evidence: Batch 1 G/H mostly selected REST (about 0.71-0.72 action frequency), achieved forage <=0.06 and water <=0.50 successes per episode, and ended at maximum toy hunger.

Batch 2 I/J increased GRAZE and DRINK actions, but received intent-based shaping when a resource was visible even when the animal only moved en route or another animal consumed it first; original reward was negative and successful water remained below the heuristic reference.
motivation.change: Use observed post-transition drive deltas for optional training shaping; never award positive shaping for an action attempt without the corresponding observed drive improvement.
motivation.evaluation: All model selection remains on unchanged original simulator reward and shared new evaluation worlds.

training.semantics: The additional target is scale times positive measured pre-to-post drive reduction for the selected action (REST shaping only when fatigue at action time is at least 0.5). No visible-resource intent bonus is used. This remains training-only; validation always scores original simulator reward.

limitations: Toy drive reductions are simulator state transitions, not cattle physiological validity.
Post-transition reward shaping can still bias training; original-reward evaluation is the only candidate acceptance score.
This protocol only authorizes batch 3 K/L; later adaptive runs require a separately versioned protocol and immutable seed allocation.
